lesson_title: Why Speeding Is Way Worse Than You Think
hook_text: Drive twice as fast and you do not carry twice the energy. You carry four times as much.
clip_script: Anything moving has kinetic energy, the energy of motion. More mass, more energy: a loaded truck carries far more than a car. But speed is the big one. Double the speed and kinetic energy goes up about four times. All of it must vanish when you brake, as heat, or in a crash, as crushed metal and injuries. That is why a pedestrian hit at thirty usually survives and at sixty often does not. Now meet the other kind: potential energy, stored energy. Water high behind a dam, a stretched catapult, the chemicals in your lunch. Watch a kid on a swing: at the top, frozen for a moment, all stored height energy. Rushing through the bottom, all speed. Back and forth, the energy keeps swapping.
visual_style: Whiteboard car with an energy bar that quadruples as the speedometer doubles; a long braking line; then a swing with a meter shifting between PE and KE.
mood: Serious hook easing into playful physics.
pacing: Punchy speed facts, a sober safety moment, a rhythmic swing finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and follow the energy on every swing and slide.
